name: manual_3d9cc9
claim: When 'cleaning up' code that calls db.execute('BEGIN IMMEDIATE') as its own explicit statement, do not assume that behavior is redundant with 'with connection:' and remove it -- Python's sqlite3 module defaults to DEFERRED transactions (an implicit BEGIN before the first write, not before the first read), so removing an explicit BEGIN IMMEDIATE silently reopens a TOCTOU race window between a transaction's read-checks and its eventual write. Caught this mid-refactor (introduced the regression, then caught it before shipping) while consolidating five near-identical connect/BEGIN-IMMEDIATE/commit blocks into one shared contextmanager -- the correct fix was moving BEGIN IMMEDIATE INTO the shared helper (so every call site keeps it automatically), not dropping it.
conditions: sqlite3 BEGIN IMMEDIATE deferred transaction TOCTOU race refactor regression atomic write lock python

decisions.notes: 2026-08-21, PT tier5_budget.py refactor (commit 1d56a095). This is a real near-miss: I removed 'db.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")' from reserve() while extracting a _transaction() helper, reasoning it was covered by the outer 'with db:' -- it was not. The atomic one-winner semantics the whole ledger module depends on (existing-key check + used-sum check happening under the SAME write lock as the eventual INSERT) would have broken silently, with no test failure, since single-threaded test runs never exercise the race window.
